dimensions.first: Professional enables sequences. Workflow-driven enrollment is a separate, higher-tier capability in the current table; the example assumes reps enroll contacts themselves.
dimensions.second: Growth includes sequences and automation. It is the more relevant comparison than an inexpensive Lite seat that cannot run the desired follow-up.

dimensions.first: A stronger candidate if the company already uses HubSpot for marketing or service and the shared operating model is valuable. Price the additional hubs and seats explicitly.
dimensions.second: A stronger candidate when the sales pipeline is the central job and the team wants to keep other business functions in existing tools.

dimensions.label: What drives adoption
dimensions.first: Clear contact ownership, a next activity, and agreed deal-stage definitions matter before sophisticated routing.
dimensions.second: The same is true here: a visually clean pipeline cannot compensate for stale deals or missing next actions.

dimensions.first: Use five existing opportunities, record the history, create next steps, and complete one follow-up path. Test the connection to the other HubSpot tools you actually intend to buy.
dimensions.second: Use the same five opportunities and follow-up path. Evaluate whether the daily operator can keep the pipeline current without duplicate entry.

caveats: A CRM subscription does not supply a qualified lead list or a lawful basis for contacting people.
Migration effort, staff training, and ongoing data hygiene are real costs even when the vendor does not bill them as onboarding.

comparisons.title: Shopify vs Etsy: what a $4,000 sales month really costs
comparisons.summary: Shopify’s platform fees can be lower once orders arrive. Etsy’s marketplace can be valuable while you find buyers. A US fee model shows exactly how much extra customer acquisition Shopify can absorb before its apparent saving disappears.
comparisons.verdict: Choose Etsy to test an eligible product in a marketplace when you do not yet have a dependable way to bring buyers to an independent store. Choose Shopify when a brand, audience, repeat customers, or a proven acquisition channel can bring those buyers to your own storefront. In the $4,000 US sales month below, modeled platform and payment fees are $185 on Shopify Basic and $425 on Etsy. That $240 gap is only $2.40 per order. Extra advertising, apps, or operational work can consume it, so lower platform fees alone are not a reason to abandon a working marketplace.

Tax, unpriced X add-ons, extra AI usage, and other services are excluded. Annual totals are paid upfront, not month by month.

pricingRows.label: Free boundary
pricingRows.first: 3 channels; 10 queued posts per channel. Published posts free up slots.
pricingRows.second: 1 brand; 20 posts per month. LinkedIn and X are excluded.

pricingRows.label: Solo paid setup
pricingRows.first: Essentials: $6 per channel/month or $60 per channel/year, for channels 1–10.
pricingRows.second: Starter, 5 brands: $25/month or $240/year. This is a fixed bundle.

pricingRows.first: Team: $12 per channel/month or $120 per channel/year, for channels 1–10.
pricingRows.second: Advanced, 15 brands: $67/month or $636/year.

scenario.title: One business, three channels, twenty-four monthly publications
assumptions: Synthetic planning example: one person, one business, three supported accounts including LinkedIn, 24 total network publications per month, no approvals.
Prepare at most ten posts per channel at once. No separate X add-on is required in this example.

calculationRows.label: Can the free plan fit?
calculationRows.first: Potentially yes: 3 channels and queue size 10. Refill slots after publication; 24 monthly publications do not alone exceed this queue allowance.
calculationRows.second: No: 24 is above 20 monthly posts, and LinkedIn is excluded on Free.

scenario.conclusion: I would test the required accounts and post formats on the smallest suitable plan first. Paying for a larger allowance is useful only when the allowance or a specific feature is the actual constraint.
scenario.caution: This is plan-fit arithmetic, not a measured comparison of reach, engagement, reliability, or time saved.

sections.title: Start with your publishing inventory
paragraphs: Write one row for every connected profile: network, account type, business, owner, planned posts, and whether another person must approve them. A single idea posted to several networks can be several publications. Confirm the counting rule before treating a content-calendar row as one unit.

Then list the formats you actually need: a text post, carousel, video, story, or another format. For each, record whether publication is direct or needs a phone reminder. A plan can fit the price and still fail your workflow if its required publishing method is unsuitable.

sections.title: A proposed side-by-side publishing test
paragraphs: Use the same approved asset and copy in both trials, and start with a draft. Verify the intended account, crop, alt text where supported, timezone, and link preview before scheduling. Make one controlled test publication that you are comfortable making public; delete or reschedule through the native service if necessary.

Record the scheduled time, actual appearance, correct account, link destination, manual steps, and any error. Test approval rejection and revision if that is part of your process. These are suggested reader tests, not experiments the publication claims to have completed.

sections.title: What “unlimited” still needs you to check
paragraphs: Buffer’s paid publishing queue is subject to fair use. Metricool also applies a fair-use policy; its 600-post monthly threshold per brand triggers review rather than acting as a guaranteed hard allowance. Neither label removes the social network’s own rules or technical limits.

Keep a fallback: save the approved copy and asset outside the scheduler, know where a failed post is reported, and record who can publish manually. Additional reach is not a result you can infer from a software subscription.

pickFirst: Your priority is a small, predictable publishing queue across a few supported accounts.
You understand the per-channel bill and need only the features of the plan selected.
pickSecond: Your profiles fit Metricool’s brand structure and its reporting workflow matters to your business.
The included bundle and required approvals or networks justify the selected paid tier.
skipBoth: Native scheduling already covers your accounts and formats.
You do not have an approved content routine yet; prepare a small reusable content brief first.

selectionChecklist: Connect the exact profile types and check required networks before paying.
Prepare one example of each needed format; distinguish direct publication from reminder-based posting.
Confirm how cross-posts count and test approval permissions if required.
Inspect a published test link and the native network result; compare reported metrics with the network’s own report.
